note: Headless, run by Claude on the bench harness (M3 Pro, DPR=2, vite 5173 + serve:static 3001). Pak: build/original/opensa REBUILT 2026-08-10 17:47 WITHOUT the procobj bake — its data/procobj.dat carries all 95 source rules (the 08-09 pak carried 9, all underwater, which is why the 2026-08-10 null-result capture could not print non-zero). ONE scene, country-dusk, 15 single-scene sweeps; 42 road cars registered (a single-scene run registers only that scene's anchors — NOT comparable to the 1219 of a full ?bench=all sweep). WHY: lod-procobj/sa-procobj 013's `opensa` perf budget (backlog band P1) — how much clutter the engine streams without hitching, which is meant to SET procObjMax, the candidate ceiling and the per-cell procObjLimit. Two lanes, and they answer different questions: CAPPED (vsync, arms a..d16) for hitching, UNCAPPED=1 (arms u-*) for cost. An uncapped arm may never be compared against a capped one. Each lane carries its own A/A pair (a/a2, u-def/u-def2) as the run-order control. RESULT, in one line: BOTH runtime knobs saturate against the authored procobj.dat MINDIST spacing long before the engine notices them — procObjLimit at 300, the density multiplier at x4 — and the layer's whole span (clutter off -> data-maximum, +10.1 % triangles) costs less than a single sweep's A/A drift on every cost column available. So this budget cannot be read off a hitch measurement, because the layer cannot be pushed into one.

runs.arm: b — ?procobj=0 (runtime clutter OFF — the positive control)
a2 — ?procobj=1 again (RUN-ORDER CONTROL for the capped lane)
u-def2 — UNCAPPED, ?procobj=1 again (RUN-ORDER CONTROL for the uncapped lane)

findings: THE KNOB IS LIVE AGAIN, and this capture is what proves the 2026-08-10 null result was a SITE failure and not an instrument one. `?procobj=0` moves country-dusk 1 206 029 -> 1 173 177 triangles (-2.72 %) and draws 830 -> 815, against this session's own A/A drift of 0.007 % (a vs a2). On the 08-09 baked pak the same arm moved 0.007 % — because convertProcObj had stripped procobj.dat to 9 underwater rules. Same code, same scene, same harness; only the pak changed.

procObjLimit SATURATES AT 300, and this half IS data-limited. 150 -> 300 adds +0.41 % of the SCENE's triangles; 300 / 600 / 1200 / 3000 then agree to within 0.015 % of each other — 60x the cap for nothing, because at cutoff 1 a cell simply does not hold 300 placements. The pool per face is `area / spacing^2` (sa-procobj-placement/009), so what runs out is the authored SPACING column. Read that +0.41 % with its SCOPE, though: 4 923 triangles against a clutter layer of 37 775, so the shipped cap of 150 is removing 13.0 % OF THE LAYER while costing 0.41 % of the scene. Small in scene terms, real in layer terms.

THE DENSITY MULTIPLIER SATURATES AT x3, AND THAT CEILING IS OURS, NOT THE DATA'S. Corrected on review before this file was read as a verdict. `scatterProcObjects` generates `area / spacing^2 x PROC_OBJ_MAX_DENSITY` candidates and gives each a lottery uniform in [0, PROC_OBJ_MAX_DENSITY); the renderer keeps `lottery < density`. PROC_OBJ_MAX_DENSITY is 3 and the runtime adapter takes the default (gta-sa-world.adapter.ts:632, no argument), so a cutoff of 3 or more keeps EVERY candidate and nothing above it can exist. The arms measure exactly that and nothing else: clutter triangles over the clutter-off baseline run 37 788 (x1) : 78 689 (x2) : 118 405 (x4) : 118 576 (x8) : 118 540 (x16) = 1 : 2.08 : 3.13 : 3.14 : 3.14 — LINEAR in the cutoff, then flat at 3. (The ~4 % over an exact 1:2:3 is species mix: a higher cutoff admits a different blend of models, and they do not carry equal triangle counts.) Raising PROC_OBJ_MAX_DENSITY makes higher densities reachable at a linear cost in candidates and scatter time — it is a knob, not a wall.

SO THE LAYER'S '+10.11 %' IS A SPAN AT TODAY'S HEADROOM, NOT A CEILING. Off (1 173 177) to the x3 maximum (1 291 753) is +10.11 % of this scene's triangles, and the shipped default delivers 2.8 pp of it — but that maximum is PROC_OBJ_MAX_DENSITY = 3, so it is what the layer costs at 3x vanilla density and not what it could ever cost. Draws move only at the on/off boundary (815 -> 830): the clutter is instanced, so it is a per-pixel cost and not a draw-count one.

NO HITCH SIGNAL EXISTS AT ANY REACHABLE SETTING. Across the 11 capped arms hitch.maxMs reads 9.7 - 36.0 ms and slowFrames 0 - 4 with NO relation to load: the two worst arms are lim600 (35.4 / 4) and d8 (36.0 / 1), while d16 — the heaviest world of the whole ladder — reads 12.3 / 0 and the A/A pair alone spans 21.9 vs 9.7. blobMaxMs, uploadMaxMs and pendingMax are 0 in every arm. So the hitch columns' own noise floor on this lane is larger than anything the layer can produce, and P1's budget CANNOT be read off them.

UNCAPPED=1 WORKS, and it retires the 'needs his display' half of P1: avgMs unpins from 8.33 to 5.42 - 5.64 and p95Ms from 9.1-9.2 to 6.7 - 7.2, at 177 - 185 fps. But it destroys the hitch columns in exchange — maxMs 148 - 196 ms and slowFrames 16 - 19 in EVERY arm including clutter-off, because the loop runs flat out and scheduling stalls dominate. Capped for hitching, uncapped for cost; neither lane answers both, and the two are not comparable.

EVEN UNCAPPED, THE LAYER IS BELOW THE NOISE. gpuMs.pass A/A (u-def 4.164 vs u-def2 3.910) is 6.5 % apart, which is WIDER than off -> max (3.952 -> 4.201, 6.3 %). On avgMs the two default arms bracket the maximum arm outright (5.643 / 5.517 vs 5.509). One sweep per arm cannot resolve this layer's cost on either column.
conclusion: P1 is ANSWERED, and the answer is that the engine is nowhere near the limiter. At 3x vanilla density — every candidate the current headroom generates — the whole clutter layer is +10.11 % of the clutter scene's triangles and still costs less than a single sweep's A/A drift on every column available, with no hitch signal at any setting. So there is no perf number to set procObjMax, the candidate ceiling or procObjLimit from, and the two knobs stop for two DIFFERENT reasons that must not be reported as one: procObjLimit stops at 300 because the authored SPACING column runs out of candidates (data), and the density multiplier stops at x3 because PROC_OBJ_MAX_DENSITY is 3 (ours, raisable at linear cost). Keep procObjLimit at 150 unless the look wants the 13 % of the layer it currently trims — 300 is the only value above it worth choosing — and treat the density ceiling as available headroom rather than as a measured maximum. What this capture does NOT cover: one scene, camera flights rather than a drive, and n=1 per arm — a streaming-shaped hitch (cells loading under continuous movement) is not sampled by any arm here, and blobMax/uploadMax/pendingMax being 0 everywhere means that pressure never arose. It also says nothing about what raising PROC_OBJ_MAX_DENSITY would cost: every arm above x3 measured the same world.
